blocks.text: Managing your travel agency itinerary software workflow

Your day as a travel agent involves constant context switching. You open a Global Distribution System like Amadeus or Sabre to check flight availability. Then you move to Excel to reconcile the costs. Finally, you draft an email in Outlook to confirm the details with your client. This fragmented environment creates friction. You might feel like you spend more time managing software than planning travel.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch to help you manage this chaos. When you hold the Option and Command keys, you can ask about anything on your screen. If you need to find a specific booking reference in a crowded spreadsheet, ask Lazur to point it out. It draws a circle around the cell for you. This saves you from scanning rows of data manually.
Reducing manual data entry and email fatigue

Manual data entry is a major pain point. You likely re-key information from booking sites into your accounting software. This process is prone to errors and takes hours every week. While you must follow your agency rules regarding client data, you can use Lazur to speed up the typing process. Hold the function key to dictate notes or email responses directly into your cursor. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the screen.

Email management is another area where you lose time. You spend about 28 percent of your workweek reading and writing emails. When you need to draft a complex itinerary, use Lazur to format your text. You can dictate the details of a flight schedule or a hotel stay. Lazur ensures the text is formatted cleanly before it lands in your email draft.

Researching visa requirements, local weather, or hotel reviews takes time. You often have multiple Chrome tabs open. Lazur can perform research in the background while you continue working in your booking software. Ask Lazur to look up current travel restrictions for a specific country. It returns a summary and a report based on the pages it finds in its own Chrome tabs. You do not need to leave your current task to get the answers you need.

blocks.text: Building your itinerary on a Mac

When you build an itinerary, you want accuracy. You might use Excel to track every leg of a trip. If you are not sure how to use a specific Excel function, ask Lazur. It explains the steps to you. You can ask, 'How do I calculate the percentage change between these two travel costs?' Lazur walks you through the steps one click at a time. It waits for you to perform each action before moving to the next.

You likely use a mix of cloud-based tools. Keeping them organized is essential. You can use Lazur to open your most-used apps or websites instantly. Simply say, 'Open my booking spreadsheet,' or 'Go to the travel supplier portal.' This keeps your desktop clean and your focus sharp. You can also use Lazur to set reminders in Apple Reminders for follow-up calls or invoice deadlines. Just hold the shortcut and say, 'Remind me to call the hotel at 2 PM.'

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in my travel software?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It points at items on your screen and guides you through processes so you can perform the actions yourself.

faq.question: Is my client data safe with Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut key. Your data is not stored or used to train AI models. You should always follow your employer's rules regarding client data and privacy.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is currently available for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel. A Windows version is planned for the future but is not available yet.

faq.question: How does the research feature work?
faq.answer: Lazur uses a dedicated Chrome extension to run research in the background. It opens its own tabs, gathers information, and provides you with a summary and report without interrupting your workflow.
